x: The Kopparam copper plates (631 CE) were issued by Pulakesin II; in these same plates Kubja Vishnuvardhana appears only as Yuvaraja. With the Maruturu inscription they record Pulakesin II's conquest of the Krishna-Godavari region. Chekurru belongs to Ammaraja I and Vipparla to Jayasimha I.

Kushmandini was the mother goddess of the Eastern Chalukyas (APPSC G2 2019 key). Hariti-putra is a matronymic, not a goddess; Kalyanakaraka is Ugradityacharya's medical treatise, not a Shaiva school (the Shaiva sects were Kapalika, Kalamukha and Pasupata); and the leading Jain centre was Potlacheruvu.

Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: the 25 inscriptions (2nd to 16th century CE) copied in the June 2026 Nallamala survey include Pottapi Chola, Eastern Chalukya and Kakatiya records. Statement 4 is wrong: the records were not of the Pallavas only, and the notes do not name the Pallavas at all. So B; C and D include the false statement 4, A misses the Kakatiyas.

The fall of the Kakatiyas in 1323 ended Telugu imperial unity; the Telugu lands stayed divided among Musunuris, Reddis, Velamas, Vijayanagara, Bahmanis and Gajapatis until the Qutb Shahis reunited the region. Vijayanagara began in 1336 and the Reddis in 1325, and Krishnadevaraya's Gajapati wars came in the 16th century.
